'''Rashid Alievich Sunyaev''' ({{langx|tt-Cyrl|Рәшит Гали улы Сөнәев}}, {{langx|ru|link=no|Раши́д Али́евич Сюня́ев}}; born 1 March 1943) is a Russian astrophysicist of [[Tatars|Tatar]] descent.<ref>{{cite news | title = Rashid Syunyaev: "I do not believe in a cosmic catastrophe in the near future..." | url = https://realnoevremya.com/articles/1721-interview-with-rashid-syunyaev-part-1 | date = 17 August 2017 | author = Timur Rakhmatullin | publisher = Realnoe Vremya}}</ref> He got his MS degree from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] (MIPT) in 1966. He became a professor at MIPT in 1974. Sunyaev was the head of the High Energy Astrophysics Department of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], and has been chief scientist of the Academy's Space Research Institute since 1992. He has also been a director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics]] in [[Garching bei München|Garching]], Germany, since 1996, and Maureen and John Hendricks Distinguished Visiting Professor in the School of Natural Sciences at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/rashid-sunyaev|title=Rashid Sunyaev|website=Institute for Advanced Study|language=en|access-date=25 June 2019}}</ref>

==Works==
Sunyaev and [[Yakov Zeldovich]] developed the theory for the evolution of density fluctuations in the early universe. They predicted the pattern of acoustic fluctuations that have been clearly seen by WMAP and other CMB experiments in the microwave sky and in the large-scale distribution of galaxies. Sunyaev and Zeldovich stated in their 1970 paper, "A detailed investigation of the spectrum of fluctuations may, in principle, lead to an understanding of the nature of initial density perturbations since a distinct periodic dependence of the spectral density of perturbations on wavelength (mass) is peculiar to adiabatic perturbations." CMB experiments have now seen this distinctive scale in temperature and polarization measurements. Large-scale structure observations have seen this scale in galaxy clustering measurements.

With Zeldovich, at the Moscow Institute of Applied Mathematics, he proposed what is known as the [[Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect]], which is due to [[electrons]] associated with gas in [[galaxy cluster]]s scattering the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Sunyaev RA|author2=Zel'dovich YB|title=The interaction of matter and radiation in a hot-model universe|journal=Astrophys. Space Sci.|volume=4|issue=3|pages=301–16|date=1969|doi=10.1007/BF00661821|bibcode=1969Ap&SS...4..301Z|s2cid=118207102}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Sunyaev RA|author2=Zel'dovich YB|title=Small-scale fluctuations of relic radiation|journal=Astrophys. Space Sci.|volume=7|issue=1|pages=3–19|date=1970|bibcode=1970Ap&SS...7....3S|doi=10.1007/BF00653471|s2cid=117050217|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00653471|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Sunyaev RA|author2=Zel'dovich YB|title=The observations of relic radiation as a test of the nature of X-ray radiation from the clusters of galaxies|journal=Comm. Astrophys. Space Phys.|volume=4|pages=173|date=1972|bibcode=1972CoASP...4..173S}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Sunyaev RA|author2=Zel'dovich YB|title=Microwave background radiation as a probe of the contemporary structure and history of the universe|journal=Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.|volume=18|issue=1|pages=537–60|date=1980|doi= 10.1146/annurev.aa.18.090180.002541|bibcode=1980ARA&A..18..537S}}</ref>

Sunyaev and [[Nikolay I. Shakura]] developed a model of [[accretion disc|accretion]] onto [[black hole]]s, from a disk,<ref>{{cite journal |author=Shakura NI |author2=Syunyaev RA|title=Black holes in binary systems. Observational appearance|journal=Astron. Astrophys.|volume=24|pages=337–55|date=1973|bibcode=1973A&A....24..337S}}</ref> and he has proposed a signature for X-radiation from matter spiraling into a black hole. He has collaborated in important studies of the early universe, including the recombination of hydrogen and the formation of the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]]. He led the team which operated the X-ray observatory attached to the [[Kvant-1]] module of the [[Mir]] [[space station]] and also the [[GRANAT]] orbiting X-ray observatory. Kvant made the first detection of X-rays from a supernova in 1987. His team is currently preparing the [[Spectrum-X-Gamma]] International Astrophysical Project and is working with [[INTEGRAL]] spacecraft data. At Garching he is working in the fields of theoretical high energy [[astrophysics]] and [[physical cosmology]] and participates in the data interpretation of the [[European Space Agency|ESA]] [[Planck spacecraft]] mission.

==Honors and awards==
[[File:Rashid Sunyaev 1980.jpg|thumb|Sunyaev in 1980]]
* 1984&nbsp;– Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]
* 1988&nbsp;– [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] for his contributions to understanding cosmic X-ray sources, especially the structure of accretion disks around black holes, the X-ray spectra of compact objects, and the Mir-based discovery of hard X-ray emission from supernova 1987A<ref>[http://www.aas.org/head/rossi/rossi.recip.html#D HEAD AAS Rossi Prize Winners] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080406082614/http://www.aas.org/head/rossi/rossi.recip.html |date=6 April 2008 }}</ref>
* 1991&nbsp;– Foreign Associate of USA [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]]
* 1995&nbsp;– [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society]]<ref>[http://www.ras.org.uk/index.php?option=content&task=view&id=268 Winners of the Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051122130144/http://www.ras.org.uk/index.php?option=content&task=view&id=268 |date=22 November 2005 }}</ref>
* 2000&nbsp;– [[Bruce Medal]] for a lifetime of outstanding research in astronomy<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.phys-astro.sonoma.edu/BruceMedalists/Sunyaev/index.html|title=The Bruce Medalists: Rashid Sunyaev|website=www.phys-astro.sonoma.edu|access-date=11 February 2018|archive-date=15 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015115552/http://www.phys-astro.sonoma.edu/brucemedalists/Sunyaev/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.astrosociety.org/membership/awards/00winners.html|title=2000 ASP Annual Award Winners|website=www.astrosociety.org|access-date=11 February 2018}}</ref>
* 2000&nbsp;– State Prize of [[Russian Federation]] for research of Black Holes and Neutron stars with [[Granat|GRANAT]] X-ray and gamma-ray astrophysical observatory in 1990–1998<ref name="a">[http://www.iki.rssi.ru/awardspr.htm Awards and best publications]. ICR RAS</ref>
* 2002&nbsp;– [[Alexander Friedman]] Prize by Russian Academy of Sciences for the publications on the reduction of brightness of cosmic microwave background radiation in the direction of clusters of [[galaxies]]<ref name=a/>
* 2003&nbsp;– [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Astrophysics|Heineman Prize]] for outstanding work in astrophysics<ref>[http://www.aas.org/grants/awards.php#heineman Dannie Heineman Prize for Astrophysics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101222143439/http://www.aas.org/grants/awards.php |date=22 December 2010 }}</ref>
* 2003&nbsp;– [[Gruber Prize in Cosmology]] for pioneering studies on the nature of the cosmic microwave background and its interaction with intervening matter that led to new cosmological models<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gruberprizes.org/GruberPrizes/Cosmology_LaureateOverview.php?awardid=22|title=The Gruber Foundation Homepage&nbsp;– The Gruber Foundation|website=www.gruberprizes.org|access-date=11 February 2018}}</ref>
* 2003&nbsp;– Member of German Academy of Natural Scientists Leopoldina
* 2004&nbsp;– Foreign Member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/6084 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160214191224/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/6084 |title=Rashid Sunyaev |publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |archive-date=14 February 2016 |access-date=14 February 2016}}</ref>
* 2007&nbsp;– International Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Rashid+Alievich+Sunyaev&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=17 May 2021|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>
* 2008&nbsp;– [[Crafoord Prize]]  for decisive contributions to high-energy astrophysics and cosmology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crafoordprize.se/press/arkivpressreleases/thecrafoordprizeinmathematicsandastronomy2008.5.744b7eb1172d57470a800015327.html|title=Crafoord Prize|website=www.crafoordprize.se|access-date=11 February 2018}}</ref>
* 2008&nbsp;– [[Henry Norris Russell Lectureship]] in 2008<ref>[http://www.aas.org/grants/awards.php#russell Henry Norris Russell Lectureship] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101222143439/http://www.aas.org/grants/awards.php |date=22 December 2010 }}</ref>
* 2008&nbsp;– [[Karl Schwarzschild Medal]] of the German [[Astronomische Gesellschaft]]<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.astronomische-gesellschaft.org/Auszeichnungen/Schwarzschild_eng.html | title = Recipients of the Karl Schwarzschild Medal | access-date = 24 September 2008 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110524132618/http://www.astronomische-gesellschaft.org/Auszeichnungen/Schwarzschild_eng.html | archive-date = 24 May 2011 }}</ref>
* 2009&nbsp;– Foreign Member of the Royal Society
* 2009&nbsp;– [[King Faisal International Prize]] for Science (Physics)
* 2011&nbsp;– [[Kyoto Prize]]<ref>[http://english.ruvr.ru/2011/06/25/52374910.html Kyoto Prize for Russian astronomer]</ref>

* 2014&nbsp;– [[Einstein Professorship]] (Chinese Academy of Sciences)
* 2019&nbsp;– [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]], (ICTP)<ref>[https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-dirac-medal/the-medallists/dirac-medallists-2019.aspx Dirac Medal 2019, ICTP]</ref>  jointly  with [[Viatcheslav Mukhanov]] and [[Alexei Starobinsky]]
* 2019&nbsp;– [[Nikolaos Kylafis|Nick Kylafis]] Lectureship<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nick Kylafis Lectureship {{!}} Institute of Astrophysics|url=https://www.ia.forth.gr/nick-kylafis-lectureship|access-date=25 October 2021|website=www.ia.forth.gr}}</ref>
* 2023&nbsp;– [[Max Planck Medal]] of the DPG<ref>[https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/max-planck-medaille/preistraeger Max Planck Medal 2023]</ref>
